title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Comprehensive Deployment and Day-2 Guide
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates the recommended deployment topologies, on-prem packaging guidance, day-2 operational playbooks, and upgrade/rollback procedures for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem). It is intended for SREs, solutions engineers, and customer platform teams responsible for deploying and operating Redwood in private environments.

Scope
- VPC-hosted private control plane with customer-managed networking.
- Air-gapped / on-prem packaging and installation patterns.
- Reference architectures for small, medium, and enterprise footprints.
- Day-2 operations (monitoring, scaling, backup/restore, incident triage).
- Upgrade and rollback procedures including canary and automated rollback triggers.
- Customer requirements library (network, IAM, hardware).

Terminology
- Control plane: Redwood control services (redwood-controller, auth, telemetry) that may run in the customer or Redwood-managed plane depending on contract.
- Data plane: Model serving runtime (redwood-runtime) that handles inference requests and KV cache.
- Agent: redwood-agent that runs on nodes to manage lifecycle and metrics export.

1) Reference Architectures
Each architecture below assumes a dedicated VPC/subnet design with segregation of control and data planes. Use separate subnets, route tables and security groups for management, compute, and storage tiers.

1.1 Small (Proof-of-Concept)
- Single availability zone.
- 2 control-plane nodes (HA proxies + controller)
- 1-2 data-plane GPU nodes (e.g., single A10 / T4 equivalent)
- Minimum external dependencies: S3-compatible object storage, DNS, and customer KMS for secrets.
- Use this for evaluation and early integration.

1.2 Production Medium
- Multi-AZ deployment (3 AZs recommended).
- 3 control-plane nodes (etcd-backed controller cluster).
- 3-6 data-plane GPU nodes spread across AZs; autoscaling group for burst capacity.
- Dedicated logging and metrics collectors (Prometheus + Thanos / Cortex).
- External integrations: customer KMS, AD/Okta SSO for SAML, private NTP.

1.3 Enterprise / Regulated
- Hybrid architecture: private on-prem inference clusters with a private control plane.
- Multi-region DR topology with read-only replicas and cross-region replication for object storage.
- Strict network egress control via firewall/NAT gateways.
- HSM integration for key operations and FIPS-validated components where required.

Reference Architecture Diagram (text)
- Management subnet: bastion, configuration management, observability exporters.
- Control subnet: redwood-controller (3 nodes), API gateway, internal load balancer.
- Data subnet: redwood-runtime nodes (GPUs), redwood-agent, KV cache layer.
- Storage subnet: object storage endpoints, snapshot targets, DB replicas.

2) On-Prem Packaging and Installation
Supported packages: OCI images + Helm charts (Kubernetes), standalone systemd packages for air-gapped bare-metal.

2.1 Kubernetes (preferred)
- Packaging: Helm chart bundle containing redwood-controller, redwood-runtime-operator, redwood-agent DaemonSet, CRDs for model pinning.
- Preflight: kubelet >= 1.26, CRI runtime compatibility (containerd recommended), ephemeral storage >= 200GB per GPU node, node labels for GPU type and network tier.
- Install steps (high level):
  1. Apply namespace and CRDs: kubectl apply -f crds.yaml
  2. Install control plane: helm install redwood-controller ./charts/controller
  3. Install agent and runtime operator: helm install redwood-runtime ./charts/runtime
  4. Verify: kubectl get pods -n redwood
  5. Upload initial model artifacts to object store and create ModelDeployment CR.

2.2 Bare-metal / Air-gapped
- Packaging: tarball with container images (OCI archive), RPM/DEB packages for redwood-agent, and a local registry manifest.
- Preflight: offline registry reachable from nodes, local S3-compatible endpoint, time sync (PTP or NTP), out-of-band KMS/HSM integration instructions.
- Install steps (high level):
  1. Load images into local registry: ./load_images.sh registry.local:5000 images.tar
  2. Install agent package and configure /etc/redwood/agent.yaml with registry and storage endpoints.
  3. Start services: systemctl enable --now redwood-agent redwood-runtime
  4. Register nodes with control plane using join token.

Hardware Recommendations (table text)
- GPU node: 1 x A100 (40GB) for large models; 2-4 x A10 / H100 equivalents for mix workloads.
- CPU: 16-64 vCPU depending on concurrency.
- RAM: 64-512 GB per GPU node.
- Disk: NVMe for local KV cache (1-2 TB recommended), separate SSD for OS (100GB).

3) Network and Security Requirements
Minimum ports and rules (example):
- Control plane API: TCP 8443 (internal LB)
- Agent heartbeat: TCP 15010
- Runtime gRPC: TCP 9000-9010 (model worker range)
- Metrics (Prometheus): TCP 9100
- KV cache replication: TCP 11211/6379 depending on backend

Network best practices:
- Use private subnets with NAT for minimal egress.
- Use security groups / firewall rules allowing only required ports between subnets.
- Enforce mTLS between control and data planes using provided cert manager.
- Restrict egress to only storage endpoints and Redwood control plane (if applicable) via firewall rules.

IAM and Secrets
- Minimum: service account per control-plane component; RBAC policies scoped to namespaces and resources.
- KMS: store encryption keys in customer-managed KMS where possible; document key rotation schedule.

4) Day-2 Operations and Runbooks
This section outlines routine and incident runbooks. All runbooks include owner, severity, preconditions, and rollback steps.

4.1 Routine operations
- Health checks (daily):
  - Verify control plane HA: kubectl get pods -n redwood -l app=controller
  - Check node heartbeats: redwoodctl nodes list --status
  - Verify KV cache hit rate > configured baseline (target 70% for chat workloads)
  - Confirm disk utilization < 75% on NVMe caches

4.2 Scaling (manual)
  1. Assess request rate and token/sec metrics from Console (window: last 15min).
  2. Increase data-plane ASG/min nodes: autoscaler scale --replicas=+2 --pool=gpu-pool
  3. Verify model deployment spreads and warms cache: redwoodctl deployments describe <id>
  4. If latency remains high after scale, investigate KV cache warming and model quantization profile.

4.3 Backup and Restore
- Snapshot schedule: daily incremental snapshots of model artifacts and weekly full snapshots of control-plane metadata. Retention: 30 days incremental, 90 days full.
- Backup verification: monthly restore test to staging.
- Restore procedure (high level):
  1. Put control plane into read-only mode: redwoodctl maintenance enable
  2. Restore DB and object storage snapshots to staging endpoint
  3. Reconfigure controller and validate state consistency
  4. Exit maintenance mode and run smoke tests

4.4 Incident Triage (control-plane failure)
Severity: P1
Owner: On-call infra SRE
Steps:
  1. Escalate and page: use standard oncall process.
  2. Check controller logs and etcd health: kubectl logs -n redwood controller-0; etcdctl endpoint health
  3. If controller degraded due to disk pressure, free disk and restart pods.
  4. If etcd corruption suspected, restore etcd snapshot per etcd restore playbook.
  5. If control plane unrecoverable, follow disaster recovery steps in Appendix A.

5) Upgrade and Rollback Procedures
Goal: ensure safe, observable upgrades with automated rollback triggers. All upgrades must be run during approved maintenance windows unless urgent security patches.

5.1 Pre-upgrade checklist
- Confirm backups completed and verified (last 24h).
- Validate cluster resource headroom (CPU, memory, GPU utilization < 60%).
- Run smoke tests against staging with canary models.
- Notify stakeholders and open change ticket with rollback plan.

5.2 Canary upgrade pattern (recommended)
  1. Create a canary pool (1-2 nodes) labeled canary=true.
  2. Deploy new runtime version to canary pool.
  3. Route 1-5% traffic to canary via routing policy.
  4. Monitor error rate, latency (p50/p95/p99), token drop, and quality regression tests for 30-60 minutes.
  5. If metrics and quality checks pass, gradually roll out to remaining pools in 10-15% increments.
  6. If any metric exceeds thresholds (error rate > 1% or p99 latency increase > 25% or quality regression detected), trigger rollback.

5.3 Automated rollback triggers
- Error rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes.
- p99 latency increase > 25% compared to baseline for 5 minutes.
- Failed health checks / crashloop restarts > 3 in 5 minutes.

5.4 Rollback procedure (high level)
  1. Immediately redirect traffic back to previous version using routing policy: redwoodctl routes set --deployment <old>
  2. Scale down new version: kubectl scale deployment/redwood-runtime --replicas=0 -n redwood
  3. Collect diagnostics bundle and open postmortem.
  4. If rollback fails or state is inconsistent, restore control-plane snapshot to pre-upgrade point and follow DR checklist.

6) Customer Requirements Library (checklist)
This checklist should be shared with customers during scoping and solutions engineering.

6.1 Network and infra
- VPC with at least 3 subnets (management, control, data)
- Private DNS entries for internal endpoints
- Allowed ports: 8443, 15010, 9000-9010, 9100, 11211/6379
- NAT/gateway for egress to object storage endpoints (or VPC endpoint)

6.2 Security and compliance
- Customer-managed KMS access and key policy for Redwood components
- SSO/SAML integration details and test account
- Audit logging retention requirements and storage endpoint

6.3 Hardware and storage
- GPU model(s) and count per node
- NVMe cache sizing and expected retention window
- Bandwidth and latency SLA between control and data subnets (target < 2ms internal)

6.4 Operational readiness
- Designated owner and oncall rotation for the deployment
- Backup frequency and retention policy confirmation
- Access method: bastion details, IP allowlist for operator CIDRs

Appendix A - DR summary
- If control plane is unrecoverable:
  1. Failover: bring up standby control plane in secondary region using snapshots.
  2. Re-point agents to standby control plane with validation token.
  3. Run validation smoke tests with a small sample of customers.

Appendix B - Useful commands and snippets
- Check node status: redwoodctl nodes list --format wide
- Deploy model: redwoodctl models deploy --name chat-3b --replicas=2 --resources gpu:A10
- Start canary routing: redwoodctl routes set --deployment <canary> --weight 5
